prerequisites: basic knowledge of materials, involving physical chemistry, thermodynamics, structure of matter, functional and mechanical properties, as taught in the LMAPR1805 course.

learning_outcomes.text: analyze an existing system and improve it
distinguish between reality and the models used to describe or modify it
understand the notion of uncertainty in the management of the project, in its realization, and in the results obtained
use the basics of a rational approach to material selection
understand the technological and scientific aspects related to the development processes for a class of materials
describe and analyze the stages of a material's life cycle
understand and choose means of microstructural characterization and measurement of basic functional and mechanical properties

syllabus_topics: Choice of a main constituent material of the object, of the device and formulation of the "materials" specifications
Critical analysis of the adequacy of the choice of this material for the specific application studied
Description of the different stages of synthesis (e.g. material balance) and shaping of the material to obtain the object
Study of the adequacy of the properties of the material with the technological, regulatory, economic, environmental constraints
Description of the properties / microstructure / implementation relationships involving the performance of experimental campaigns to be defined
Description of the techniques for measuring properties
Comparison of material properties with competing materials
Proposal of a more efficient, more economical and/or more ecological alternative solution based on a life cycle analysis
teaching_methods: Group project work with supervision by tutors
Access to scientific laboratories for material characterization

assessment_methods.method: Group project (execution, written presentations, oral presentations/interactions, work organization, reflective posture, mastering concepts)
Individual written assessment outside the term

assessment_rules: Students are assessed as a group (oral and written) and individually (written exam). The project mark may be individualized based on student involvement and cannot be repeated in the second term. The weighting of the individual assessment in the final mark is 25% if passed, but increases if failed, with a specific formula: weight = 1 - 0.75 * (mark - 6)/4 for marks between 6 and 10, and 100% for marks less than or equal to 6. The second session consists of an individual examination, possibly with prior individual work.
